body:
Path: `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md` (authoring rule 2, :338–:341) | published skill — Tier H, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (`skills/**` in `MANDATORY_TIER_GLOBS`) | graded by `domain:skills#2`

Filed by the `domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024, session `session_01QCdUBjM47SxioST9z5Zwdf`) out of the #19248 round (PR #19352), where it arrived as a **read-only prose sweep** the seat commissioned after the docs-drift check disclaimed coverage. ⛔ Filed bare: `finding` only; `domain:*`, type and priority are triage's.

Dedupe words: `skills/objectstack-ui pages.md` · `fail at install` · `instance-global doc names` · `ADR-0048 §3.4 retired` · `collide across packages`.

## The shape

`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md`, authoring rule 2 (**Namespace-prefixed filename**). Read verbatim from `origin/main`:

> Names share one flat, instance-global space with the URL, so a bare `user_guide` would **collide across packages and fail at install** (ADR-0048).

⭐ **It cites ADR-0048 as its authority for a claim ADR-0048 retired.** §3.4, quoted verbatim:

> The cross-package **throw is retired**; two distinct packages coexist on the same bare name by construction.

## Three separable errors, each measured

| # | the text says | what is true |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | doc names share *"one flat, instance-global space"* | ⛔ replaced by §3.1/§3.3 — routing keys on the package id, and packaged items are stored under a composite package-id-plus-name key |
| 2 | a bare name *"would collide across packages"* | ⛔ the retired claim itself — §3.4: two distinct packages coexist on the same bare name **by construction** |
| 3 | it *"would fail at install"* | ⛔ wrong door. The install gate (§3.2) refuses on `manifest.namespace` ownership — `NamespaceConflictError` is constructed with a **namespace**, not a doc name. A bare doc name is refused at **BUILD**, by `docs/namespace-prefix` |

## ⚠️ Why this placement is the worst of the three the sweep looked at

`skills/**` is the **customer-published catalog an AI author reads while writing docs**. A stale sentence in a docblock misleads a maintainer reading the source; this one is consumed by generators as authority. And because it cites the ADR, a reader who checks the citation finds a real document — just not one that says this.

⭐ Contrast, and it is the reason this card exists rather than a wider one: `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx:76-82` — the hand-written prose page that states the same rule — is **already correct**, and refutes the retired claim explicitly: *"two installed packages may each ship a doc with the same bare name and coexist — neither silently overwrites the other."* ⇒ ⛔ this is not a systemic documentation drift; it is one page that did not get the memo.

## Scope

⛔ **Not fixed in PR #19352, and not this lane's to fix.** `skills/**` is a **Tier H governed surface** — the tier reserves the landing. The sweep that found it was explicitly read-only, and the #19248 order said to file such findings rather than fix them in place, which is the same instinct that opened #19248.

## First act

Decide whether rule 2's *reason* should be restated (namespace prefixing is **authoring hygiene** plus a build-time `docs/namespace-prefix` refusal) or simply dropped to the enforceable fact (the stem must start with the package namespace, enforced at build). ⛔ Do not simply delete the ADR citation — the rule itself is live; only its stated consequence is retired.
